analysis.title: Impartial analysis of Measure T

text: IMPARTIAL ANALYSIS OF MEASURE [TBDI

The Board of Trustees of the Pacifica School District (District) proposes to renew and extend an expiring special parcel tax to support various educational purposes, as outlined below. The District currently has in place a parcel tax (Measure D) that will expire June 30, 2027. This Measure, if approved by voters, would extend the parcel tax for an additional ten years, starting July 1, 2027 and ending June 30, 2037, in the amount of $118 per parcel. The amount of the tax is subject to annual adjustment for inflation based on the "Consumer Price Index for all Urban Consumers San Francisco Area" published by the U.S. Department of Labor, Bureau of Labor Statistics, and is estimated to raise $1,300,000 each year.

The proposed parcel tax applies to any unit of real property wholly or partially in the District that receives a separate property tax bill from San Mateo County tax collection officials. Any person 65 years of age or older who owns and occupies a parcel within the District may apply for an exemption from the tax. An exemption is also available to any person who receives Supplemental Security Income for a disability, regardless of age, and to any person who receives Social Security Disability Insurance benefits, regardless of age, whose annual income does not exceed 250% of the 2012 federal poverty guidelines.
The stated purposes of the proposed parcel tax are to:

Enhance core academic programs, including math, science, history, reading, and writing; Support art, music, and other electives; Attract and retain qualified teachers and staff; Maintain classroom computer and technology instruction; Strengthen school library programs; and Maintain programs to support struggling students.

The proceeds of the parcel tax will be placed in a special account and used only for the purposes described in the Measure, which do not include administrator salaries or benefits. A report accounting for the amount of parcel tax revenues collected and expended, and the status of any projects or programs funded by the tax, will be filed with the Board of Trustees no later than December 31 of each year, commencing December 31, 2027. The District's existing Citizens' Oversight Committee will continue to review the expenditures of the parcel tax.
The District's appropriations limit shall be increased annually, if necessary, to ensure the revenue from the tax may be spent for the purposes authorized.

A "yes" vote on this Measure would impose on property within the District an annual parcel tax of $118, subject to annual adjustment for inflation, for ten years beginning July 1, 2027, for the purposes listed above.
A "no" vote on this Measure would not allow the parcel tax to be levied.
This Measure passes if at least two-thirds of those voting on the Measure vote "yes".

text: S OFFICER
Argument in Favor of Measure

Vote Yes on Measure _ to renew local education funding that protects excellent academic programs, including library services and outdoor education, and retains qualified teachers without raising taxes by a single penny.
Pacifica's elementary and middie schools are a source of. community pride, yet they remain among the lowest-funded schools in San Mateo County.

Measure provides dedicated local funding for qualified teachers. librarians and programs that support student success in English, math. science and technology. It also preserves Outdoor Education for every fifth-grade student. Without Measure . Pacifica School District would have to reduce teachers. librarians and critical educational programs.
Measure continues Pacifica's tradition of supporting local schools with funding that stays in our community and cannot be taken by the state or used for administrators.
Vote Yes on _ : Strong Schools Build Strong Communities

Attract and retain qualified teachers Enhance core academic programs Support struggling students • Strengthen library services Maintain technology instruction Support outstanding art, music and electives critical to a well-rounded education Measure _ Is Fiscally Accountable and Does Not Increase Taxes

• Every dollar stays in Pacifica schools and cannot be taken by the state • No money can be used for administrators' salaries • An inde.pendent Citizens' Oversight Committee has ensured responsible spending for more than two decades • Homeowners age 65 and older remain eligible for an exemption Our local elementary and middie schools are an integral part of our community. Please join parents, teachers and community leaders in protecting quality education, strengthening our community and investing in Pacifica's future. Vote Yes on Measure

text: Measure T is not a new tax; Yes on Measure T renews existing funding dedicated to programs such as 5th grade Outdoor Education, library services for all students, and a mental health counselor. If Measure T does not pass, we will have to cut an additional $1.4 million from our schools.
Accountability safeguards such as a citizens' oversight committee, public spending disclosures, and annual audits have and will continue to ensure responsible use of these dedicated funds.

Pacifica schools are consistently among the lowest-funded per student, forcing teachers and classified staff to repeatedly fight for fair compensation. In San Mateo County, an annual income of $117,500 for an individual is considered low income, yet Pacifica teachers start at just $57,000, while classified staff and librarians earn even less. 52

Pacifica students need thriving local educators, not a revolving door of teachers leaving our community for a living wage in other districts. If we expect students to perform better in school, we must retain qualified teachers, preserve counselors and librarians. Libraries play a critical role in building literacy, strengthening reading comprehension, and giving students the skills they need to succeed across every subject.

The author of the argument against Measure T does not live in the Pacifica community, routinely opposes school ballot measures and cherry-picks facts. He doesn't have students in our schools, and he should not speak for Pacificans. We can give Pacifica's children the strong educational foundation they deserve by voting Yes on Measure T.
